stories.text: At a Moscow conference, Ruchir gave a frank presentation about Russia's weak small-business sector while Vladimir Putin was present. Russian press then attacked him, his Morgan Stanley boss urged him to leave, and he left the country.

insights.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

quotes.text: The simplest ideas typically outshine the complicated ones.
quotes.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
quotes.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

quotes.text: What matters in reality is making things work.
quotes.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
quotes.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

quotes.text: Answering questions will be seen as a commodity.
quotes.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
quotes.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

quotes.text: You got to have AIs that not just help you do research, but help you make transactions natively.
quotes.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
quotes.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

ideas.text: Build real-time voice AI that handles Indian languages, accents and dialects well.
ideas.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
ideas.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

ideas.text: Build a platform where people can create, deploy and share software tailored to their own needs without managing its infrastructure.
ideas.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
ideas.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

ideas.text: Aggregate Indian podcasts with live interaction, translation and AI-generated edits tailored to a listener's topic of interest.
ideas.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
ideas.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

ideas.text: Start with a useful AI product and users, then use open-source models for post-training before attempting original models and data-center investment.

stories.text: At IIT, Aravind learned about machine learning through a Kaggle contest, tried several algorithms and won it. He then pursued machine-learning research.
stories.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
stories.lesson: A practical problem can provide an entry into a new field.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

stories.text: During his OpenAI internship, Aravind presented research ideas to Ilya Sutskever, who told him they were too complicated and described a simpler route centered on generative AI, reinforcement learning and compute.
stories.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
stories.lesson: Aravind came to value methods that work at scale over ideas that merely seem sophisticated.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

episodes.raw_title: Ep# 15 | WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

insights.text: A uniform emissions-reduction timetable would lock lower-emitting developing countries into a lower per-person emissions level, according to an objection Navroz heard in early climate negotiations.
insights.speaker: Navroz
insights.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

insights.text: Navroz argues that Indian climate measures gain support when they also solve development problems, as public transport and decentralized energy can.
insights.speaker: Navroz
insights.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

insights.text: Sunita says farmers, fishers and others who work with the land recognize climate changes even if they do not use the term 'climate change.'
insights.speaker: Sunita
insights.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

insights.text: Sunita argues that climate solutions need enough speed and scale to have a visible effect; she cites Delhi's rapid adoption of CNG vehicles.
insights.speaker: Sunita
insights.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

insights.text: Bhumi says film productions can bring temporary jobs to remote villages while leaving pollution and disruption behind.
insights.speaker: Bhumi
insights.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

insights.text: Mirik identifies bioenergy, waste management and circularity as connected opportunities suited to India's local supply chains and operating conditions.
insights.speaker: Mirik
insights.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

data_points.metric: IPCC assessment cycle
data_points.speaker: Navroz
data_points.context: A new group of authors begins another assessment after each cycle.
data_points.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

data_points.metric: Review comments received by Navroz's IPCC chapter
data_points.speaker: Navroz
data_points.context: He cited the volume of scrutiny in each of three review rounds.
data_points.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

data_points.metric: New CNG vehicles introduced in Delhi
data_points.speaker: Sunita
data_points.context: Sunita used the rollout as an example of implementing an environmental solution at scale.
data_points.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

data_points.metric: Electricity cost cited for mini grids
data_points.speaker: Sunita
data_points.context: She said this cost makes replacing grid electricity difficult without support.
data_points.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

quotes.text: They may not have the fancy word that you and I have, call it climate change.
quotes.speaker: Sunita
quotes.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

quotes.text: We're not protecting trees, we're protecting our toilet ground.
quotes.speaker: Sunita
quotes.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

quotes.text: You've got to find ways of bringing a development problem in conversation with the climate angle.
quotes.speaker: Navroz
quotes.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

ideas.text: Build bioenergy, waste-management and circular-economy businesses around India's local supply chains.
ideas.speaker: Mirik
ideas.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

ideas.text: Provide decentralized renewable-energy services that improve rural productivity, such as agricultural processing or cold storage for medicines and vaccines.
ideas.speaker: Navroz
ideas.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

ideas.text: Use frugal engineering to turn discarded materials into affordable products, as in the example of making incense sticks from flowers discarded by temples.
ideas.speaker: Sunita
ideas.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

stories.text: Sunita visited women involved in the Chipko movement expecting to hear about protecting trees. They told her the trees also protected their toilet ground and their right to use forest resources, changing how she understood environmental work.

insights.text: A founder should recognize warning signs and cut losses before commitment to a failing business turns into denial; Kiran applies this lesson to Kingfisher Airlines.

insights.text: Biocon moved from enzymes into biopharmaceuticals by reusing its fermentation capabilities for higher-value products.
insights.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
insights.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

insights.text: An IPO gave Biocon valued stock that could be monetized or used in acquisitions, beyond the cash raised at listing.
insights.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
insights.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

insights.text: Unilever's ownership taught Biocon global manufacturing, reporting, regulatory and intellectual-property practices.
insights.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
insights.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

insights.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
insights.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

insights.text: Building biosimilars over a long period let Biocon absorb costs that would sharply affect an established pharmaceutical firm's current earnings if it entered now.
insights.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
insights.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

insights.text: India needs more research spending and curiosity-driven education to turn its young population into innovation capacity.
insights.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
insights.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

quotes.text: You've got to have hunger in your belly and you've got to have an idea which you think is exciting.
quotes.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
quotes.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

quotes.text: Don't be wedded to a historic business if that business can be monetized and if someone else can make a bigger business of that business.
quotes.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
quotes.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

quotes.text: Wealth has never been about money. Wealth has been about value creation.
quotes.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
quotes.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

quotes.text: Today we are followers, we are not innovators.
quotes.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
quotes.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

ideas.text: Use fermentation platforms developed for enzymes to manufacture biopharmaceuticals, including statins and insulin.

ideas.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

ideas.text: Add research-linked incentives to India's pharmaceutical policy alongside production-linked incentives.

ideas.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

ideas.text: Build biotechnology ventures in genomics, cell and gene therapy, diagnostics, or personalized medicine.
ideas.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
ideas.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

stories.text: In 1978, Les Hawkins tracked Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw down in Baroda before her train to Delhi and persuaded her to start an Indian enzyme venture instead of taking a brewing job in Scotland.

stories.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

stories.text: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw told Vijay Mallya to downsize Kingfisher Airlines during its crisis, but he continued trying to fund a larger airline as losses and debt grew.

stories.lesson: Act on early signs of failure rather than financing escalating losses.
stories.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

stories.text: John sold his Chelsea townhouse investment and helped raise two million dollars so he and Kiran could buy Unilever's 30 percent stake in Biocon.

stories.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

stories.speaker: Aravind Srinivas
stories.lesson: Aravind came to value methods that work at scale over ideas that merely seem sophisticated.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath ft. Perplexity CEO, Aravind Srinivas | WTF Online Ep 1.

stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Netflix Co-CEO, Ted Sarandos | People by WTF | Ep. 10

stories.episode_title: Sam Altman x Nikhil Kamath: How to Win When AI Changes Everything | People by WTF | Episode 13

stories.episode_title: WTF does it take to Build Influence Today? Nikhil w/ Nuseir, Tanmay, Prajakta & Ranveer

stories.episode_title: From Iran to Uber CEO | Nikhil Kamath x Dara Khosrowshahi | People by WTF | Ep. 14

stories.episode_title: From Iran to Uber CEO | Nikhil Kamath x Dara Khosrowshahi | People by WTF | Ep. 14

stories.episode_title: A.R. Rahman: The Genius Who Took Indian Music Global | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF | Ep 15

stories.episode_title: WTF is Climate Change? Nikhil ft. Sunita, Bhumi, Navroz and Mirik

stories.episode_title: Elon Musk: A Different Conversation w/ Nikhil Kamath | Full Episode | People by WTF Ep. 16

stories.episode_title: What character "flaws" make the best entrepreneurs? Nikhil ft.Ritesh, Ghazal and Manish

stories.lesson: Targeted teaching can help a developing game team build new capabilities.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Gaming in India? | Career, Investment, Entrepreneurship

stories.text: Animesh said SuperGaming invited him and Mortal to see Indus and give feedback well before launch; that early involvement made him willing to discuss the game later.
stories.speaker: Animesh
stories.lesson: Bring creators into development early to earn informed support.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Gaming in India? | Career, Investment, Entrepreneurship

stories.text: Harari describes Denmark helping the US after the September 11 attacks as an example of a relationship that held when one partner was in crisis.
stories.speaker: Yuval Noah Harari
stories.lesson: An alliance's value becomes clear when help is needed.
stories.episode_title: Yuval Noah Harari: Stories, Power & Why Truth Doesn't Matter | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Harari recalls Trump's response to questions about Putin's broken promises: Trump said the promises had been made to Obama and Biden, rather than to him.
stories.speaker: Yuval Noah Harari
stories.lesson: Personalizing state commitments undermines institutional continuity.
stories.episode_title: Yuval Noah Harari: Stories, Power & Why Truth Doesn't Matter | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: While studying protein biomarkers, Amodei found biological systems dauntingly complex; seeing early neural-network work led him toward AI as a possible tool for biological discovery.
stories.speaker: Dario Amodei
stories.lesson: A hard problem in one field can motivate a career shift into another.
stories.episode_title: The AI Tsunami is Here & Society Isn't Ready | Dario Amodei x Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Amodei says Anthropic developed Claude Code internally because its staff wrote code, then built a more approachable interface after seeing non-coders struggle with the terminal.
stories.speaker: Dario Amodei
stories.lesson: Internal use and observed user friction can guide product development.
stories.episode_title: The AI Tsunami is Here & Society Isn't Ready | Dario Amodei x Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Minakshi says she wanted to bartend after hotel school but found women were barred from doing so in some Indian states; she moved into beverage marketing and later opened Cocktails and Dreams Speakeasy with Yangdup Lama.
stories.speaker: Minakshi
stories.lesson: A blocked career path can lead to another route into the same industry.
stories.episode_title: WTF, Alcohol is a $70B Business in India? | Nikhil Kamath explores Gaps & Opportunities

stories.text: The Goa Brewing founder says an IPA tasted on a flight to New York prompted him to visit breweries throughout his US trip and pursue a different kind of beer in India.
stories.speaker: Unattributed
stories.lesson: A product discovery became the starting point for a brewing venture.
stories.episode_title: WTF, Alcohol is a $70B Business in India? | Nikhil Kamath explores Gaps & Opportunities

stories.text: An event organizer says he met his wife at one of his own events and had earlier created SpottedClub.com to photograph nightlife across Indian cities.
stories.speaker: Unattributed
stories.lesson: Event organizing led to a broader entertainment business.
stories.episode_title: WTF, Alcohol is a $70B Business in India? | Nikhil Kamath explores Gaps & Opportunities

stories.text: Chamath says a company he helped start was sold to Nvidia for $20 billion, yet a screenshot of the first large payment left him focused on newer problems rather than celebrating.
stories.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
stories.lesson: A major financial outcome need not feel like a personal endpoint.
stories.episode_title: Pain, Power & The Game Nobody Wins | Chamath Palihapitiya x Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Chamath recalls Elon Musk showing him a Gigafactory schematic and calling it 'the machine that makes the machine,' an idea that later shaped his software-factory project.
stories.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
stories.lesson: A manufacturing concept can inspire a software business model.
stories.episode_title: Pain, Power & The Game Nobody Wins | Chamath Palihapitiya x Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Chamath says leveraged, high-risk investments created a liquidity crisis that forced him to sell Tesla shares; repeated losses led him to change his position-sizing approach.
stories.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
stories.lesson: Position size and liquidity matter alongside conviction.
stories.episode_title: Pain, Power & The Game Nobody Wins | Chamath Palihapitiya x Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Kriti says her mother put her into kathak classes after seeing her dance at a college event when she was five; she disliked the classes then but later valued the training.
stories.speaker: Kriti Sanon
stories.lesson: Early practice can become useful long after it ends.
stories.episode_title: WTF is “Making it” in an Offbeat Career? Nikhil Kamath Ft. Kriti Sanon, Badshah & KL Rahul

stories.text: Rahul says he asked for cricket coaching from childhood, but his father waited until he was 11 to enroll him in a camp.
stories.speaker: KL Rahul
stories.lesson: His interest in cricket preceded formal coaching.
stories.episode_title: WTF is “Making it” in an Offbeat Career? Nikhil Kamath Ft. Kriti Sanon, Badshah & KL Rahul

stories.text: Badshah says he produced 'Saturday Saturday' for local release in 2012; after Varun and director Shashank heard it in a Chandigarh club, Dharma contacted him about using it in a film.
stories.speaker: Badshah
stories.lesson: A locally released song reached film audiences through club play.
stories.episode_title: WTF is “Making it” in an Offbeat Career? Nikhil Kamath Ft. Kriti Sanon, Badshah & KL Rahul

stories.text: Brett says he sold his AI recruiting marketplace Vetery to the Adecco Group in 2017, then started Archer Aviation to build electric aircraft.
stories.speaker: Brett Adcock
stories.lesson: Experience integrating hardware and software carried into his later robotics work.
stories.episode_title: Humanoids Cost as Much as an SUV Now | Nikhil Kamath x Brett Adcock | WTF Online Ep 2

stories.text: Brett says Figure 2 has worked every workday at a BMW production line, giving Figure data on autonomous operation, interventions and failures.
stories.speaker: Brett Adcock
stories.lesson: A live deployment reveals problems that demonstrations cannot.
stories.episode_title: Humanoids Cost as Much as an SUV Now | Nikhil Kamath x Brett Adcock | WTF Online Ep 2

stories.text: Brett says he has kept a Figure robot in his home for months to test tasks, while supervising it around his children.
stories.speaker: Brett Adcock
stories.lesson: Home testing has not yet established the safety record he wants for unsupervised use.
stories.episode_title: Humanoids Cost as Much as an SUV Now | Nikhil Kamath x Brett Adcock | WTF Online Ep 2

stories.text: Ranbir says he left a résumé outside Sanjay Leela Bhansali's office after Devdas; Bhansali called him the next day, and Ranbir later assisted on Black.
stories.speaker: Ranbir Kapoor
stories.lesson: He pursued the filmmaker he most wanted to learn from.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Ranbir Kapoor | People by WTF Ep #2

stories.text: Ranbir recalls Ayan telling him several days into Wake Up Sid that he was playing the part like a hero rather than a character.
stories.speaker: Ranbir Kapoor
stories.lesson: The correction changed how he approached later roles.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Ranbir Kapoor | People by WTF Ep #2

stories.text: Ranbir says he produced Jagga Jasoos, which did poorly at the box office, and concluded that producing required skills he did not have.
stories.speaker: Ranbir Kapoor
stories.lesson: Success in acting did not automatically translate into producing.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Ranbir Kapoor | People by WTF Ep #2

stories.text: Tanmay says he began posting jokes on Twitter in 2009, reached his first 10,000 followers, and met the people who formed AIB through Twitter.
stories.speaker: Tanmay Bhat
stories.lesson: Publishing consistently helped him build both an audience and creative relationships.
stories.episode_title: Secrets of Social Media Success, Mental Health & Distribution Hacks - 3 OGs Reveal All

stories.text: Umang says his driver took a job in Dubai and then sent him a LinkedIn request because Instagram felt intimidating to him.
stories.speaker: Umang Bedi
stories.lesson: A platform's portrayed lifestyle can affect who feels comfortable using it.
stories.episode_title: Secrets of Social Media Success, Mental Health & Distribution Hacks - 3 OGs Reveal All

stories.text: Umang says Dailyhunt had about a month's cash left in March 2020, then raised funding on March 28.
stories.speaker: Umang Bedi
stories.lesson: He describes how close the company came to running out of cash.
stories.episode_title: Secrets of Social Media Success, Mental Health & Distribution Hacks - 3 OGs Reveal All

stories.text: Ray says he saved money from caddying, bought a cheap stock that was then acquired and tripled, and became interested in markets at age 12.
stories.speaker: Ray Dalio
stories.lesson: An early gain drew him into investing, though he says the trade's reasoning made no sense.
stories.episode_title: WTF Is Wealth? Ray Dalio Breaks It Down w/ Nikhil Kamath | WTF is Finance Ep 2

stories.text: Ray says he was clerking at the New York Stock Exchange in 1971 when President Nixon ended the dollar's convertibility into gold.
stories.speaker: Ray Dalio
stories.lesson: The event shaped his attention to money and claims on it.
stories.episode_title: WTF Is Wealth? Ray Dalio Breaks It Down w/ Nikhil Kamath | WTF is Finance Ep 2

stories.text: Ray says his grandchildren sell hot cider in a park and learn about equipment costs, unit costs, margins and recovering their initial spending.
stories.speaker: Ray Dalio
stories.lesson: A small venture can teach the mechanics of business.
stories.episode_title: WTF Is Wealth? Ray Dalio Breaks It Down w/ Nikhil Kamath | WTF is Finance Ep 2

stories.text: Rishi Sunak said his appointment as UK prime minister fell on Diwali and his daughter's birthday; the Downing Street Diwali reception days later was when the significance of being the first British Asian and Hindu prime minister hit him.
stories.speaker: Rishi Sunak
stories.lesson: A public milestone can carry a special responsibility to the community it represents.
stories.episode_title: Rishi Sunak & Akshata Murty: Power, Identity & Why Patience Beats Ambition | Nikhil | People by WTF

stories.text: Rishi Sunak described William Wilberforce campaigning as a backbench MP for about 20 years before Parliament passed a slave-trade bill, then about 20 more years before slavery was declared illegal.
stories.speaker: Rishi Sunak
stories.lesson: Long institutional campaigns can deliver major change without the top office.
stories.episode_title: Rishi Sunak & Akshata Murty: Power, Identity & Why Patience Beats Ambition | Nikhil | People by WTF

stories.text: Akshata Murty said that, at 23, she wrote her Stanford application essay about Mumbai's monsoon and how unequal shelter shaped her interest in equality of opportunity.
stories.speaker: Akshata Murty
stories.lesson: A concrete experience can clarify a lasting social aim.
stories.episode_title: Rishi Sunak & Akshata Murty: Power, Identity & Why Patience Beats Ambition | Nikhil | People by WTF

stories.text: Irfan said his family put him in charge of selling their Infantry Cross Road property around 1980; reinvesting the proceeds and flipping plots led him into real estate.
stories.speaker: Irfan
stories.lesson: Handling a real transaction taught him the business before he became a developer.
stories.episode_title: WTF are Indian Real Estate Giants Up To? Nikhil ft. Irfan, Nirupa, & Karan

stories.text: Irfan said his first Bangalore mall opened in February 2004, shortly after his father died, and drew daily crowds that reached tens of thousands because organized retail was new to visitors.
stories.speaker: Irfan
stories.lesson: A new retail format can create demand beyond initial forecasts.
stories.episode_title: WTF are Indian Real Estate Giants Up To? Nikhil ft. Irfan, Nirupa, & Karan

stories.text: Karan said his coworking team initially spent more to copy spaces from abroad, then localized its supply chain and lowered its fit-out spending per square foot.
stories.speaker: Karan
stories.lesson: Localizing procurement can improve unit economics without giving up the product.
stories.episode_title: WTF are Indian Real Estate Giants Up To? Nikhil ft. Irfan, Nirupa, & Karan

stories.text: Ajay Banga said HDFC began with an IFC investment and went on to become a major private bank and a force in India's mortgage market.
stories.speaker: Ajay Banga
stories.lesson: Early development finance can help create an enduring private financial institution.
stories.episode_title: The World Bank President On Why Jobs Fix Everything | Ajay Banga x Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Ajay Banga described visiting farmers' cooperatives in Uttar Pradesh using a Google open platform to identify a diseased leaf and find a low-cost insecticide through their cooperative.
stories.speaker: Ajay Banga
stories.lesson: Simple digital tools can turn agricultural information into a practical decision.
stories.episode_title: The World Bank President On Why Jobs Fix Everything | Ajay Banga x Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Ajay Banga said he left candidacy for Citi's chief executive job to lead the much smaller Mastercard, a risk he cited while discussing how to act on luck.
stories.speaker: Ajay Banga
stories.lesson: A smaller organization can be the better career opportunity when its trajectory is stronger.
stories.episode_title: The World Bank President On Why Jobs Fix Everything | Ajay Banga x Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Nithin Kamath said he completed an Ironman in October or November while feeling at his fittest, then suffered a stroke in January.
stories.speaker: Nithin Kamath
stories.lesson: Fitness efforts and monitoring do not remove all health uncertainty.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Longevity? | Nikhil ft. Nithin Kamath, Bryan Johnson, Prashanth, Jitendra & Seema

stories.text: Bryan Johnson said he took an air purifier into a Mumbai hotel gym, measured poor air there, and decided that exercising hard in that room would increase exposure to pollutants.
stories.speaker: Bryan Johnson
stories.lesson: Indoor exercise space can have harmful air even when it looks clean.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Longevity? | Nikhil ft. Nithin Kamath, Bryan Johnson, Prashanth, Jitendra & Seema

stories.text: Seema described getting a breast-cancer diagnosis, searching across hospitals for the right oncologist, undergoing surgery, and finding that her mental state received little attention.
stories.speaker: Seema
stories.lesson: Cancer navigation should include specialist choice and emotional support.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Longevity? | Nikhil ft. Nithin Kamath, Bryan Johnson, Prashanth, Jitendra & Seema

stories.text: Martin Escobari said his father fled a Bolivian farm during the 1952 revolution after the house was burned and thousands of sheep were slaughtered; he then worked as a public-service doctor in rural Bolivia.
stories.speaker: Martin Escobari
stories.lesson: Family experience of upheaval shaped Martin's view of fragility and resilience.
stories.episode_title: Martin Escobari: Trauma, Chaos & Three Industries Worth $100B | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Martin Escobari said his Brazilian ecommerce company had filed for an IPO, but the market crashed three weeks before it; after layoffs and a failed $25 million sale, the company cut growth to reach profitability and later went public.
stories.speaker: Martin Escobari
stories.lesson: Financial discipline can keep a company alive when capital markets close.
stories.episode_title: Martin Escobari: Trauma, Chaos & Three Industries Worth $100B | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Arian said he emailed Sam Altman as a teenager with examples of projects he had built; Altman first replied that he was busy, and Arian's later follow-ups led to a meeting in San Francisco.
stories.speaker: Arian
stories.lesson: Specific work samples and persistence can make cold outreach effective.
stories.episode_title: Martin Escobari: Trauma, Chaos & Three Industries Worth $100B | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Matt and his wife launched Blue Tokai in 2012 from a bedroom in her parents' house, roasting on a 500-gram tabletop roaster after persuading growers to sell them export-quality beans.
stories.speaker: Matt
stories.lesson: A premium category can start with a small supply experiment.
stories.episode_title: WTF are Craft Beverages? Nikhil ft. the Founders of Blue Tokai, Subko, Svami, and Mossant

stories.text: Anish and Swami's cofounders took their tonic to restaurants, opened it beside Schweppes for tastings, and found that repeat orders depended on the product's taste.
stories.speaker: Anish
stories.lesson: Direct comparison and repeat demand matter more than an initial listing.
stories.episode_title: WTF are Craft Beverages? Nikhil ft. the Founders of Blue Tokai, Subko, Svami, and Mossant

stories.text: Nikos recalled children lining Cyprus's streets to welcome Indira Gandhi during her 1982 or 1983 visit, which he remembered as a major event for the young republic.
stories.speaker: Nikos Christodoulides
stories.lesson: Cyprus and India have a long diplomatic connection.
stories.episode_title: Nikos Christodoulides on Why India Must Lead What Comes Next | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: After moving from academia into politics, Nikos found that reading meeting minutes had not captured raised voices and body language in the room.
stories.speaker: Nikos Christodoulides
stories.lesson: Written records omit information needed in live negotiations.
stories.episode_title: Nikos Christodoulides on Why India Must Lead What Comes Next | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF

stories.text: Rahul adapted a Nokia machine-to-machine device to power Indian payphone booths with a SIM card; the business later expanded from a few crore rupees annually to around 100 crore rupees.
stories.speaker: Rahul Sharma
stories.lesson: Repurposing existing technology for a local use case can create a market.
stories.episode_title: WTF are Consumer Electronics? | Nikhil ft. Carl Pei, Rahul Sharma & Amit Khatri

stories.text: Amit and his cousin Gaurav launched iPhone covers under Noise, failed with unsold inventory, then moved to Xiaomi accessories and later smartwatches.
stories.speaker: Amit Khatri
stories.lesson: Move to a category with a real demand gap when an initial product fails.
stories.episode_title: WTF are Consumer Electronics? | Nikhil ft. Carl Pei, Rahul Sharma & Amit Khatri

stories.text: Nikon joined Hall for enterprise communication one week before Slack launched; Atlassian later bought Hall.
stories.speaker: Nikon
stories.lesson: Choosing the right market does not ensure choosing the winning company.
stories.episode_title: Inside Silicon Valley’s VC Playbook | WTF is Venture Capital? - 2025 Edition | Ep. 24

stories.text: At Opendoor, Nikon saw the firm cut 35% of staff in 2020 and go public six months later.
stories.speaker: Nikon
stories.lesson: A startup's operating conditions can reverse quickly.
stories.episode_title: Inside Silicon Valley’s VC Playbook | WTF is Venture Capital? - 2025 Edition | Ep. 24

stories.text: At Reliance Brands, Bhakti first sold Timberland shoes in a Mumbai store and learned the three-box rule of showing a footwear customer multiple options; her family bought a pair during a sale.
stories.speaker: Bhakti
stories.lesson: Frontline retail work teaches how purchase decisions happen.
stories.episode_title: Tira, Bombay Shaving Co., Inde Wild | WTF is Fueling India’s Beauty & Skincare Revolution? | Ep. 25

stories.text: Deepa named Inde Wild's Chumpy hair oil after the familiar hair-oiling ritual despite objections from her team, and it became a household product for the brand.
stories.speaker: Deepa
stories.lesson: A recognizable ritual can anchor a product story.
stories.episode_title: Tira, Bombay Shaving Co., Inde Wild | WTF is Fueling India’s Beauty & Skincare Revolution? | Ep. 25

stories.text: Rajiv Juneja worked in his brother's Meerut medical store during school holidays, became a medical representative for ten years, and started Mankind in 1995.
stories.speaker: Rajiv Juneja
stories.lesson: Direct experience of pharmacies, doctors, and sales shaped Mankind's distribution strategy.
stories.episode_title: Two Pharma Giants Who'd Never Met | Mankind & Dr. Reddy's | WTF is Pharma?

stories.text: After Dr. Anji Reddy's co-founder at Cheminor Drugs parted ways, he called G. V. Prasad; Prasad took the CEO role in 1990, and Cheminor later merged with Dr. Reddy's.
stories.speaker: Unattributed
stories.lesson: A trusted operator helped scale and consolidate the group.
stories.episode_title: Two Pharma Giants Who'd Never Met | Mankind & Dr. Reddy's | WTF is Pharma?

stories.text: Nandan Nilekani joined the Indian government in 2009 to lead Aadhaar, promised 600 million IDs before leaving, and says the project reached that number when he stepped down.
stories.speaker: Nandan Nilekani
stories.lesson: A measurable enrollment target helped drive a new public infrastructure project.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Nandan Nilekani | People by WTF | Ep #3

stories.text: Jio used Aadhaar eKYC after its 2016 launch to enroll a million mobile customers a day toward a goal of 100 million in six months.
stories.speaker: Nandan Nilekani
stories.lesson: Fast digital identity checks enabled rapid distribution.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Nandan Nilekani | People by WTF | Ep #3

stories.text: Kishore Biyani visited small-town bazaars before launching Big Bazaar and opened three stores in 22 days to create scale and the bustle he wanted.
stories.speaker: Kishore Biyani
stories.lesson: Local retail behavior shaped the format and launch pace.
stories.episode_title: WTF is E-commerce: Kishore Biyani, Udaan & Meesho Founders Reveal What Sells and What Doesn’t

stories.text: Future Group staff went to Tirupati temple to study how it managed queues, water, and waiting for the large crowds at Big Bazaar.
stories.speaker: Kishore Biyani
stories.lesson: Operational lessons can come from outside one's industry.
stories.episode_title: WTF is E-commerce: Kishore Biyani, Udaan & Meesho Founders Reveal What Sells and What Doesn’t

stories.text: Sujeet Kumar joined Flipkart in 2008 when it was still a proprietorship taking only a few book orders, built its supply-chain operation including Ekart, and left in 2016 to start Udaan.
stories.speaker: Sujeet Kumar
stories.lesson: Early logistics capability supported e-commerce scale.
stories.episode_title: WTF is E-commerce: Kishore Biyani, Udaan & Meesho Founders Reveal What Sells and What Doesn’t

stories.text: Yann LeCun studied electrical engineering in Paris, pursued independent AI projects with mathematics professors, and became drawn into research rather than following a formal computer-science route.
stories.speaker: Yann LeCun
stories.lesson: Cross-disciplinary projects opened his path into AI research.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Artificial Intelligence Really? | Yann LeCun x Nikhil Kamath  | People by WTF Ep #4

stories.text: One participant said his team integrated ChatGPT into a creator interface so users could click an idea button and request help with content, including poems and images of Virat Kohli or Rohit Sharma.
stories.speaker: Unattributed
stories.lesson: Putting AI in an existing creation workflow makes assistance immediately accessible.
stories.episode_title: WTF is ChatGPT: Heaven or Hell? | w/ Nikhil, Varun Mayya, Tanmay, Umang & Aprameya

stories.text: A participant said his team made a company whose system can speak to customers in real time, train on an intended caller's voice, and handle several calls in parallel.
stories.speaker: Unattributed
stories.lesson: Voice generation can scale conversations, while business decisions still need accountability.
stories.episode_title: WTF is ChatGPT: Heaven or Hell? | w/ Nikhil, Varun Mayya, Tanmay, Umang & Aprameya

stories.text: Gaurav Munjal asked his friend Roman, newly through the UPSC examination, to record preparation videos before training; those videos brought Unacademy about a million views.
stories.speaker: Gaurav Munjal
stories.lesson: A single high-demand teaching format can reveal a larger product opportunity.
stories.episode_title: EdTech What’s Broken, What’s Next? With Nikhil, Ronnie Screwvala , Gaurav Munjal & Jay Kotak

stories.text: Ronnie Screwvala said UTV's first five movies failed, yet he continued because film was needed to build a consumer media brand.
stories.speaker: Ronnie Screwvala
stories.lesson: A new channel may require several failures before its strategic value appears.
stories.episode_title: EdTech What’s Broken, What’s Next? With Nikhil, Ronnie Screwvala , Gaurav Munjal & Jay Kotak

stories.text: Gaurav Munjal said Resonance in Jaipur rejected him from Ashish Arora's batch after an entrance test; Arora later joined Unacademy.
stories.speaker: Gaurav Munjal
stories.lesson: Digital education can broaden access to teachers once restricted to selected batches.
stories.episode_title: EdTech What’s Broken, What’s Next? With Nikhil, Ronnie Screwvala , Gaurav Munjal & Jay Kotak

stories.text: Kumar Mangalam Birla worked beside his father through meetings for long days while studying for his CA; when his father began testing his understanding, he realized Kumar had absorbed the discussions.
stories.speaker: Kumar Mangalam Birla
stories.lesson: Direct exposure and feedback built confidence before he took responsibility.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Kumar Birla | People by WTF Ep #5

stories.text: Kumar Mangalam Birla spent a year on the shop floor at Century Textiles to learn manufacturing controls and operations.
stories.speaker: Kumar Mangalam Birla
stories.lesson: Operational experience can ground later leadership decisions.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Kumar Birla | People by WTF Ep #5

stories.text: A scholarship named for his father enabled a woman from a conservative family to continue her education when her parents could only afford to educate her brother.
stories.speaker: Kumar Mangalam Birla
stories.lesson: Scholarships can alter the choices created by unequal household resources.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x Kumar Birla | People by WTF Ep #5

stories.text: Modi read a military-school advertisement in his village, ordered the English prospectus by money order and asked headmaster Rasbihari Maniyar to explain it; his father said the family could not afford to send him.
stories.speaker: Narendra Modi
stories.lesson: Money constrained an early ambition despite his initiative.
stories.episode_title: People with The Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi x Nikhil Kamath | Episode 6 | By WTF

stories.text: While driving an RSS Jeep back from Ukai Dam, Modi switched off the engine to save petrol on a slope and lost control of braking; the passengers escaped harm.
stories.speaker: Narendra Modi
stories.lesson: A failed shortcut became a direct lesson in risk.
stories.episode_title: People with The Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi x Nikhil Kamath | Episode 6 | By WTF

stories.text: After becoming Gujarat chief minister, Modi sent officers to earthquake-affected districts; they returned identifying rules that blocked progress, and he told them to change those rules.
stories.speaker: Narendra Modi
stories.lesson: Field visits can reveal and remove administrative bottlenecks.
stories.episode_title: People with The Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi x Nikhil Kamath | Episode 6 | By WTF

stories.text: Mukesh Bansal said Myntra sold personalized T-shirts online for years without strong demand, pivoted to fashion in 2011 and merged with Flipkart in 2014.
stories.speaker: Mukesh Bansal
stories.lesson: Experimentation can expose a stronger market than the original niche.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Health? ft. Nikhil Kamath, Suniel Shetty, Nithin Kamath and Mukesh Bansal

stories.text: Nithin Kamath said his wife Seema's breast-cancer diagnosis in 2020 led him to examine his diet and stop treating exercise as enough by itself.
stories.speaker: Nithin Kamath
stories.lesson: A family health event changed his own health priorities.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Health? ft. Nikhil Kamath, Suniel Shetty, Nithin Kamath and Mukesh Bansal

stories.text: Suniel Shetty stepped away from cinema while caring for his father, then received a call about a major fitness show the morning after his father died.
stories.speaker: Suniel Shetty
stories.lesson: He treated the call as a reason to return to work on his own terms.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Health? ft. Nikhil Kamath, Suniel Shetty, Nithin Kamath and Mukesh Bansal

stories.text: Christopher Luxon brought New Zealand's largest prime-ministerial delegation to India, including business and community representatives and a kapa haka performing-arts team.
stories.speaker: Christopher Luxon
stories.lesson: Cultural and business visits can deepen ties between countries.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x NZ PM Christopher Luxon | People by WTF Ep #7

stories.text: Luxon said he moved abroad at 24 with his wife Amanda, spent 16 years overseas and raised their two children away from extended family support.
stories.speaker: Christopher Luxon
stories.lesson: The experience made his immediate family central to his identity.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x NZ PM Christopher Luxon | People by WTF Ep #7

stories.text: In 1978, Les Hawkins tracked Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw down in Baroda before her train to Delhi and persuaded her to start an Indian enzyme venture instead of taking a brewing job in Scotland.
stories.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
stories.lesson: A credible partner can open an entrepreneurial path when conventional employers refuse one.
stories.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

stories.text: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw told Vijay Mallya to downsize Kingfisher Airlines during its crisis, but he continued trying to fund a larger airline as losses and debt grew.
stories.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
stories.lesson: Act on early signs of failure rather than financing escalating losses.
stories.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

stories.text: John sold his Chelsea townhouse investment and helped raise two million dollars so he and Kiran could buy Unilever's 30 percent stake in Biocon.
stories.speaker: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
stories.lesson: A contractual preemptive right enabled the founders to regain ownership.
stories.episode_title: Who is Kiran Mazumdar Shaw Really? And WTF is Biotech?

stories.text: As a child, Bill Gates worked out that his grandmother won card games by remembering every card played; she made him discover her method himself.
stories.speaker: Bill Gates
stories.lesson: Patiently staying with confusion helped him understand a difficult pattern.
stories.episode_title: Bill Gates x Nikhil Kamath Part 2 | People by WTF | Ep.8

stories.text: On Microsoft retreats, Gates kept warning other leaders about threats to the company's survival even when they did not share his concern.
stories.speaker: Bill Gates
stories.lesson: Fear of losing a dominant position can drive intense competitive behavior.
stories.episode_title: Bill Gates x Nikhil Kamath Part 2 | People by WTF | Ep.8

stories.text: Ajay Bijli renovated Priya Cinema after finding that his family's trucking business did not suit him; he then turned underused cinemas into multiplexes and opened his first in 1997.
stories.speaker: Ajay Bijli
stories.lesson: Existing cinema properties became a path to expansion before malls were available.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Going on in the World of Content | w/ Nikhil, Ajay Bijli, Vijay S. & Sajith S.

stories.text: Sajith Sivanandan's parents mortgaged their 1100-square-foot home for his studies at the Asian Institute of Management in Manila, prompting him to take study seriously.
stories.speaker: Sajith Sivanandan
stories.lesson: A family's financial commitment changed his sense of responsibility.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Going on in the World of Content | w/ Nikhil, Ajay Bijli, Vijay S. & Sajith S.

stories.text: Vijay Subramaniam began by managing a school band, then interned at Mahesh Bhupathi's Global Sports after it rented space in his family's house.
stories.speaker: Vijay Subramaniam
stories.lesson: Early entertainment work and a nearby opportunity led him into talent management.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Going on in the World of Content | w/ Nikhil, Ajay Bijli, Vijay S. & Sajith S.

stories.text: Neal Mohan started a small software venture in high school in Lucknow, building software for fellow students and teachers.
stories.speaker: Neal Mohan
stories.lesson: His interest in technology began before his media career.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x YouTube CEO, Neal Mohan | People by WTF Ep. 9

stories.text: Mohan saw creator-led studios run by Rhett and Link and Alan Chicken Chow near Disney's Burbank studio, producing YouTube-style shows in 10,000-square-foot facilities.
stories.speaker: Neal Mohan
stories.lesson: Creators can build their own production infrastructure.
stories.episode_title: Nikhil Kamath x YouTube CEO, Neal Mohan | People by WTF Ep. 9

stories.text: Rajan Anandan said he and his younger brother survived violence in Sri Lanka because they could speak both Sinhala and Tamil when people were being pulled from cars nearby.
stories.speaker: Rajan Anandan
stories.lesson: He says the experience made him grateful and changed how he handles business setbacks.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Venture Capital? Ft. Nikhil, Nithin, Rajan A., Prashanth P. & Karthik R.

stories.text: Karthik Reddy used his savings for several angel checks, then invested for a businessman whose company he had helped sell before helping found Blume Ventures.
stories.speaker: Karthik Reddy
stories.lesson: Small personal investments and an operating relationship led into full-time venture work.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Venture Capital? Ft. Nikhil, Nithin, Rajan A., Prashanth P. & Karthik R.

stories.text: Prashanth Prakash recalled his father leaving HMT to start a small supplier for ITI and struggling to raise his first five or ten lakh rupees.
stories.speaker: Prashanth Prakash
stories.lesson: Seeing a parent start a factory gave him an early view of entrepreneurship.
stories.episode_title: WTF is Venture Capital? Ft. Nikhil, Nithin, Rajan A., Prashanth P. & Karthik R.
